test_cases.title: SD Card Initialization Returns Success on Healthy Card
test_cases.setup: POSIX build with backing-file SD mock pointing to a freshly created empty image. SD library root structure allocated by caller.
procedure: Invoke SdLib_New()/Init() against the mock SD backend.
Capture the returned JUNO_STATUS_T value.
Query the library state to confirm initialized flag is set.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Init returns JUNO_STATUS_SUCCESS and the library reports an initialized state suitable for subsequent writes.

test_cases.title: SD Card Initialization Reports Failure When Card Absent
test_cases.setup: POSIX build with SD mock configured to simulate no card present (CMD0/CMD8 negative response).
procedure: Invoke SdLib_Init() against the absent-card mock.
Capture the returned status code.
Verify the library does not transition to initialized state.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Init returns a non-success JUNO_STATUS_T error and the library remains in an uninitialized state.

test_cases.title: Capacity Reported After Successful Initialization
test_cases.setup: POSIX SD mock configured with a known capacity (e.g., 512 MiB image file).
procedure: Initialize the SD library against the mock.
Call SdLib_GetCapacity() (or equivalent capacity accessor).
Compare the returned byte count to the known mock image size.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Capacity accessor returns SUCCESS and the reported byte count equals the configured mock capacity.

test_cases.title: New Run Directory Created on First Power-On
test_cases.setup: POSIX SD mock pointing at an empty FAT image (no existing run directories).
procedure: Initialize the SD library.
Invoke run-directory creation (e.g., SdLib_OpenRun()).
Enumerate top-level directories in the SD image after the call.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Exactly one new run directory exists on the SD image and the library reports its name as the active run.

test_cases.title: Distinct Run Directory Created on Subsequent Power-On
test_cases.setup: POSIX SD mock with a FAT image already containing one prior run directory from an earlier session.
procedure: Initialize the SD library against the pre-populated image.
Invoke run-directory creation.
Enumerate top-level directories and compare names against the pre-existing set.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: A new run directory is created with a name distinct from every prior run directory on the card.

test_cases.title: Prior Run Directories Preserved Across Power-On
test_cases.setup: POSIX SD mock with a FAT image containing two prior run directories, each with known files and bytes.
procedure: Snapshot the contents (file list and byte hashes) of each prior run directory.
Initialize the SD library and create a new run directory.
Write some bytes into the new run directory and close it.
Re-snapshot the contents of the prior run directories.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Every file in every prior run directory has unchanged size and unchanged byte hash after the new session completes.

test_cases.title: Sequential Byte Writes Land in Current Run Directory File
test_cases.setup: POSIX SD mock with empty image. SD library initialized and a run directory opened.
procedure: Open a log file inside the current run directory via the library API.
Issue three sequential SdLib_Write() calls with chunks of 256, 1024, and 4096 bytes.
Flush/close the file.
Read the file from the SD image and compare bytes to the concatenation of the three input chunks.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: The on-disk file contains exactly the concatenated input bytes in the order written and resides under the current run directory.

test_cases.title: Bytes Written Verbatim Without Modification
test_cases.setup: POSIX SD mock; SD library initialized; run directory opened; log file open.
procedure: Generate a 64 KiB buffer containing every byte value 0x00..0xFF repeating, plus embedded 0x00 and 0xFF runs.
Write the buffer in a single SdLib_Write() call.
Flush and close the file.
Read the file back and compare byte-for-byte against the original buffer.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Every byte read from disk matches the corresponding source byte; no insertions, deletions, escaping, or transformations occur.

test_cases.title: Sustained Logging Throughput on Pico 2 Hardware
test_cases.setup: Pico 2 flashed with FT1 FSW image. Class 10 (or better) SD card inserted. Serial terminal open at 115200 baud. Stopwatch or host logger ready.
procedure: Power on the Pico 2 and wait for POST to complete on the serial terminal.
Trigger the throughput demo command (or run the production logging path with all sensors enabled).
Run the system for 120 seconds while it logs full-rate sensor, nav, and event data.
Observe the serial terminal for any backpressure, dropped-write, or queue-full warnings.
Power down the Pico 2, remove the SD card, and read the active run directory on a host PC.
Compute the total bytes written and divide by elapsed run duration to obtain sustained throughput.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: No backpressure or dropped-write warnings appear on serial; sustained throughput meets or exceeds the FT1 full-rate logging budget recorded in the design doc.

expected_artifacts.name: throughput_serial_log.txt
expected_artifacts.description: Serial terminal capture for the 120 s run showing absence of backpressure warnings.

expected_artifacts.name: run_dir_byte_count.txt
expected_artifacts.description: Host-side report of total bytes written, run duration, and computed sustained throughput.

test_cases.title: Writes Continue After Injected Transient Failure
test_cases.setup: POSIX SD mock that returns a transient write error on the Nth write call and succeeds on subsequent calls. SD library initialized; log file open.
procedure: Issue write A (expect success).
Issue write B with the mock primed to return a transient error (expect failure status).
Issue write C with the mock returning success.
Flush and close, then read the file from the image.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Write C returns SUCCESS and its bytes appear on disk; the library does not enter a permanently-disabled state after write B fails.

test_cases.title: Failed Write Returns Non-Success Status
test_cases.setup: POSIX SD mock configured to fail a specific write call with a simulated CRC or bus error. SD library initialized; log file open.
procedure: Issue an SdLib_Write() call against the failure-primed mock.
Capture the returned JUNO_STATUS_T value.
Verify the failing call's bytes are not reported as committed by the library.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: The failing write returns a non-success JUNO_STATUS_T error code distinct from JUNO_STATUS_SUCCESS.

test_cases.title: Health Status Reflects Recent Write Success
test_cases.setup: POSIX SD mock with programmable per-call results. SD library initialized; log file open; health accessor available.
procedure: Issue several successful writes; query SdLib_GetHealth().
Inject a write failure on the next call; query health again.
Issue several successful writes after the failure; query health again.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Health reports healthy after the success run, transitions to unhealthy after the failure, and returns to healthy after sustained subsequent successes.

test_cases.title: POSIX Build Exposes Same Write API As Flight Build
test_cases.setup: POSIX build of sd_lib linked into the test harness with a backing-file SD image. Identical caller code as the flight build's logging path.
procedure: Invoke the same Init, OpenRun, OpenFile, Write, and Close call sequence used by the flight FSW.
Write a fixed reference payload of 16 KiB.
Read back the resulting file from the POSIX backing image.
Compare the on-disk file bytes against the reference payload.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Every call returns SUCCESS and the on-disk bytes match the reference payload, demonstrating API and behavior parity with the flight build.

test_cases.title: Run Directory Layout Matches Between POSIX and Flight
test_cases.setup: POSIX build of sd_lib with empty backing image. Naming/sequencing seed identical to the flight build's first power-on.
procedure: Run the same Init + OpenRun + Close sequence twice in a row, simulating two power-ons.
Enumerate the resulting run directories from the backing image.
Compare the directory naming pattern and sequencing rule against the documented flight behavior.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Two distinct run directories appear, named per the same pattern and sequence as documented for the Pico 2 flight build.

test_cases.title: Identical Inputs Produce Identical On-Disk Bytes
test_cases.setup: POSIX SD mock with two independent backing images, both starting empty. Fixed seed for any naming counters.
procedure: Run the SD library Init/OpenRun/Write/Close sequence against image A with a fixed input payload.
Repeat the identical sequence against image B with the same payload and seed.
Read the active run directory file back from each image.
Compute and compare byte hashes (or do a byte-for-byte memcmp) of the two files.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: The two on-disk files are byte-for-byte identical, demonstrating deterministic write behavior given identical inputs.
